This implies a chain of interactions where Plantagineoside C may modulate the activity of the EP4 receptor, which is involved in signaling pathways related to inflammation and cell proliferation. The involvement of 10-O-Methylprotosappanin B, a known inhibitor of the Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3, further supports the notion that Plantagineoside C may influence the transporter's function. The integrated evidence suggests that Plantagineoside C could exert its effects by modulating the EP4 receptor, which in turn affects the activity of the transporter, potentially altering the transport of organic anions. The mechanism is supported by the presence of a direct interaction between Plantagineoside C and the EP4 receptor, and the subsequent inhibition of the transporter by 10-O-Methylprotosappanin B. The relationship is biologically plausible, though the exact nature of the interaction between Plantagineoside C and the transporter remains to be fully elucidated.
